outcome: Treatment options utilized (Laparotomy with scar excision and repair, Laparoscopic scar excision and repair, Systemic MXT, USG guided dilation and evacuation, Laparotomy and scar excision and IU tamponade, Suction and evacuation, Suction and evacuation + IU tamponade, Hysteroscopic removal)
cohort: The study included 16 women presenting to antenatal OPD or casualty with amenorrhoea, abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, a positive urine pregnancy test, a history of previous LSCS, and TVS-documented or intraoperative features suggestive of caesarean scar pregnancy.
finding: The study found that the majority of patients with cesarean scar pregnancy were aged 25-30 years, 37% were 3rd gravida, and 56.2% had a history of two previous LSCS, with the majority diagnosed at 8-10 weeks gestational age, leading to various treatment approaches.
mod_finding: Majority of patients (56.2%) in the study had a history of previous two LSCS, indicating a strong association between prior cesarean sections and the development of cesarean scar pregnancy.
gest_age: Majority of patients (43.7%) had gestational age of 8-10 weeks.
